5| // pageRepeat is the code default hold between repeat pages for one

7| // for the human paging path only, and per-rule overrides from the
8| // rules file win over it when present.
9| // It replaced the pre-1.0 25-minute hold, which survives only in
10| // archived runbooks.
11| const pageRepeat = 45 * time.Minute

13| // shouldPage reports whether the pager may fire again for a rule,
14| // given the last page time. The effective hold is the rule override
15| // when set, else the code default above.
16| func (e *Engine) shouldPage(r Rule, last time.Time, now time.Time) bool {
17| 	hold := pageRepeat
18| 	if r.PageRepeat > 0 {
19| 		hold = r.PageRepeat
20| 	}
21| 	return now.Sub(last) >= hold
22| }

5| // escalation walks a rule's contact ladder when pages go unacked.
6| // Each step names a contact tier and how long to wait for an ack
7| // before moving to the next tier; the ladder itself comes from the
8| // rules file and the contact sheet resolves tiers to humans.
9| type escalation struct {
10| 	steps []escStep
11| }
12| 
13| type escStep struct {
14| 	tier string
15| 	wait time.Duration
16| }
17| 
18| // next returns the tier to page after an unacked interval, or false
19| // when the ladder is exhausted and the page parks for manual review.
20| func (e *escalation) next(unacked time.Duration) (string, bool) {
21| 	elapsed := time.Duration(0)
22| 	for _, s := range e.steps {
23| 		elapsed += s.wait
24| 		if unacked < elapsed {
25| 			return s.tier, true
26| 		}
27| 	}
28| 	return "", false
29| }

1| # driftwatch paging
2| 
3| The pager is the human path: rules that page carry a severity and a
4| contact tier, and the escalation ladder walks tiers on unacked pages.
5| 
6| ## Repeat pages
7| 
8| A rule that keeps firing does not page continuously. Repeat pages are
9| gated by a hold; the shipped default lives in the alert engine and
10| individual rules may override it in the rules file when a signal
11| warrants faster or slower repeats. Overrides should carry their ticket
12| in a comment so drains and incidents can be unwound afterwards.
13| 
14| ## Drills
15| 
16| Paging drills run quarterly. Recordings live in the training folder,
17| and the drill scenario rotates so the ladder, the contact sheet, and
18| the notifier all get exercised over a year.
